comment: Baseline of secret findings that are ALREADY in this repository's git history (issue #211).
Why a baseline instead of `continue-on-error: true`: the CI step used to be
non-blocking so the known historical hits would not leave it permanently red,
which also meant a genuinely NEW leak would never fail the build. This file
names the known hits individually, so anything that is not on the list blocks.
Why not `git filter-repo`: the commits are pushed and cloned, so the strings
stay readable in every existing clone and in GitHub's object cache even after
a rewrite. The credential has to be revoked or deactivated for the exposure to
end; the DingTalk credentials here belong to a virtual/test organization (see
the closing analysis on issue #211), so nothing is live.
Fingerprint = sha256(rule + NUL + file + NUL + startLine), first 16 hex chars.
Every component comes from content already frozen in the git history, so the
value is identical in every clone. The secret itself is deliberately NOT part
of the fingerprint and NOT stored here — a baseline that embedded the plaintext
would be a second copy of the leak.
Line numbers are stable because the files are gone from the working tree; the
findings refer to blobs inside historical commits, which never change. If a
fingerprint here stops matching, that is a signal the history was rewritten,
not that the entry is stale: the scan fails until this file is regenerated
with `node scripts/scan-git-history-secrets.mjs --write-baseline`.
Every entry below was verified by hand against the matched text before being
accepted. Do not add entries to silence a finding you have not read.
